## 固定收益開場主論點

美國就業成長大幅放緩，降低聯準會再次升息的急迫性，帶動美國公債殖利率曲線在7月2日轉陡，卻未形成全面的長天期債券漲勢。縮短交易時段的日資料顯示，2年期殖利率下跌3.9個基點至4.138%，10年期微升0.5個基點至4.485%，30年期則上升1.5個基點至4.986%。2年期與10年期利差擴大4.4個基點至34.7個基點，2年期與30年期利差增加5.4個基點至84.8個基點。美國獨立紀念日前夕，市場依SIFMA建議於美東時間下午2時提前收市。

6月非農就業人數僅增加57,000人，不及113,000人的預測中位數，前2個月數據也遭下修。儘管如此，勞動參與率下降，使失業率降至4.2%。這種好壞參半的組合促使投資人降低近期升息風險，卻未將數據視為經濟驟然下滑的證據。市場隱含的7月升息機率由數據公布前約33%降至約20%，完全反映一次升息1碼的時點則由10月延後至12月。

殖利率曲線的反應呈現了這項區別。就業數據疲弱與空頭回補有利於政策敏感的短端，但10年期實質殖利率仍上升0.3個基點至2.246%，10年期損益兩平通膨率也增加0.2個基點至2.239%。初領失業救濟金人數維持低檔、工廠出貨增加，加上6月就業報告中的失業率下降，使疲弱的非農就業表面數字不再單純。投資人只是延後預期中的聯準會行動，並未放棄限制性政策可能持續的看法。

油價進一步緩解了眼前的通膨衝擊，但並未再度崩跌。WTI與布蘭特原油一度觸及2月以來低點，收盤仍分別上漲0.16%至$68.69及0.32%至$71.80；兩者單月跌幅均超過24%。美元指數下跌0.52%至100.86，黃金期貨上漲1.09%至$4,112.70。這些走勢與聯準會無須急於行動的路徑一致，但長端未能上漲，顯示近期政策風險降低並未消除實質利率、供給或期限溢價壓力。

日本市場進一步強化全球長天期債券所受的制約。10年期公債標售需求疲弱，推動指標殖利率上升7個基點至2.77%，20年期殖利率則上升9.5個基點至3.76%。投資人同時面對財政擴張、日圓嚴重貶值，以及日本央行漸進升息可能讓通膨壓力持續的疑慮。標售前公布的企業狀況轉強，短觀調查中的長期通膨預期也創新高；即使政府傾向審慎，這些發展仍提高日本央行再次行動的理由。

風險資產的反應分歧，並非典型的成長恐慌。標普500指數大致持平，道瓊指數上漲1.1%，但那斯達克100指數下跌1.61%，費城半導體指數重挫5.44%。主要上市信用債基金小幅上漲，新興市場貨幣則受惠於美元走弱。整體風險偏好穩定、科技股賣壓卻高度集中，這種分化對債市格外重要，因為AI相關借款人目前已占投資級債券供給的一大部分。就業數據轉弱減輕了聯準會的政策制約，卻未能回答資本密集的科技投資週期、主權債發行及持續的通膨風險，是否會讓長端殖利率維持高檔。

## 就業數據將市場預期的聯準會升息時點推向12月

6月非農就業人數增加57,000人，低於調查預測區間內除一項以外的所有預測，前2個月數據也遭下修。這波放緩打斷了年初以來較強的招聘動能，其中休閒與餐旅業錄得2020年以來最大就業降幅，提供了比整體數字更具體的疲弱跡象。

不過，失業率降至4.2%，使這份報告不能被解讀為明確惡化。勞動參與率下滑，讓失業率在招聘放緩之際仍能下降。對貨幣政策而言，這種組合削弱立即升息的理由，卻不足以證明勞動市場正廣泛收縮；後者通常才會帶動整條美國公債殖利率曲線持續走低。

每週失業救濟金數據也凸顯招聘放慢與廣泛裁員之間的差別。截至6月27日當週，初領失業救濟金人數減少1,000人至215,000人，前一週數據由215,000人上修至216,000人；4週移動平均減少2,500人至222,000人。截至6月20日當週，持續領取失業救濟金人數增加2,000人至181.4萬人，4週移動平均增加10,750人至180.3萬人，續領失業救濟金率則維持1.2%。

這些數據顯示，失業者重新找到工作所需的時間可能略有拉長，但企業尚未以經濟快速收縮時常見的速度裁員。因此，短端上漲之際，較長天期殖利率仍然堅挺：數據降低近期升息機率的程度，明顯大於其縮短限制性政策預期持續時間的程度。

空頭回補放大了2年期公債的漲勢。聯準會6月會議後，18位決策官員中有9位預測2026年至少升息一次，市場因此圍繞7月可能升息累積了偏空部位。隨著7月升息機率降至約20%，原先預期就業報告較強的投資人有理由回補短端空單。2年期公債的漲勢既反映影響聯準會反應函數的證據改變，也受到數據公布前既有部位的推動。

舊金山聯準銀行總裁Mary Daly在就業報告公布後另行釋出政策訊號。她表示，目前政策立場略具限制性，應能推動通膨下降。她樂見美國與伊朗停火後油價回落，但強調前景仍異常不明朗，若通膨持續，可能需要更強力的因應。這番立場保留了有條件升息的可能，並未認同市場對非農就業數據最鴿派的解讀。

聯準會主席Kevin Warsh正在檢討央行的運作及分析架構，Daly也反對改變聯準會的政策目標。她表示，聯準會可以更新評估經濟的方式，但不應更動充分就業與物價穩定的目標。這項區別之所以重要，是因為聯準會偏好的通膨指標5月較上年同期上升4.1%，創2023年4月以來最快增幅。一份疲弱的非農就業報告固然降低匆促行動的必要，卻未消除促使決策官員在6月預測升息的通膨問題。

5月工廠數據也說明，就業不及預期不等於整體經濟突然失速。新訂單在4月增加5.3%後，5月減少1.3%、即$85億，降至$6,574億；出貨則增加1.6%至$6,532億，未完成訂單增加0.6%至$1兆5,795億，存貨增加0.2%至$9,620億。未完成訂單與出貨比由6.95降至6.91，存貨與出貨比則由1.49降至1.47。

結果顯示，4月激增後的新需求轉弱，但生產與未完成訂單仍在成長。配合初領失業救濟金人數維持低檔，數據較支持成長放緩，而非經濟突然崩跌。6月就業報告最明顯改變的是聯準會預期行動的時點：市場仍反映2026年升息1碼，但已不再預期12月以前行動。

縮短交易時段內，美國公債交易活動下降。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$8,484億、共316,299筆，較7月1日減少31.5%。名目附息債券交易量下降28.9%至$6,353億，TIPS交易量減少43.1%至$153億。降幅與假期前縮短交易時段一致，但短端重新定價的幅度仍足以使殖利率曲線明顯轉陡。

## 日本標售疲弱凸顯漸進正常化的代價

日本10年期公債標售是當日最明顯的主權債需求失望。投標倍數由上次標售的3.53降至3.13，也低於過去一年平均的3.33。標售尾差擴至4月以來最大，最低得標價格也遠低於標售前預估。造市商承接量僅略高於規定配額，顯示其不願在當時殖利率水準大幅吸收指標天期債券。

次級市場立即作出反應，10年期JGB殖利率上升7個基點至2.77%，20年期殖利率上升9.5個基點至3.76%。這波弱勢並非只是日本央行6月將利率升至1%後的機械式反應；投資人也要求市場針對財政擴張、日圓持續貶值，以及日本央行可能落後於通膨進程的風險提供補償。

首相高市早苗的政府正推動大規模支出計畫，並設定在2040年4月開始的會計年度將名目GDP擴大至$6.8兆的目標。投資人也在觀察政府是否會暫停對食品與飲料徵收消費稅。這些政策企圖出現之際，政府債務已超過GDP的200%，殖利率上升也逐步提高既有債務的再融資成本。

日圓疲弱使困境更加棘手。在隨後的亞洲交易時段，日圓在兌美元161.30附近交易，此前已觸及1986年以來未見的水準。匯率貶值推高進口能源與原料成本，而政治上要求漸進升息的壓力，又使日本央行難以迅速縮小利差。今年稍早的干預曾令日圓短暫升值，卻未消除造成貶值的貨幣政策與財政條件。

國內最新證據也使央行愈來愈難維持審慎立場。儘管中東爆發衝突，6月短觀調查顯示企業信心升至8年來最高。企業財務狀況指數一年來首次改善，大型企業也表示發行商業本票的條件轉佳。這份調查因而削弱了先前日本央行升息已經損害企業融資的說法。

短觀調查中的長期通膨預期升至2.6%，創2014年該系列開始以來新高。市場目前認為日本央行在10月前再次升息的機率超過60%；此前經濟學家大多預期約每隔6個月行動一次，意味下一次升息在12月。部分預測者已將10月列為基本情境，並認為9月升息的可能性正在增加。

政治訊號仍指向相反方向。高市一向支持寬鬆政策，她任命的日本央行委員佐藤綾乃與淺田東一郎也被視為傾向較寬鬆的政策設定。淺田是6月升息時唯一投下反對票的委員，佐藤則表示通膨常態尚未穩固建立。政府經濟方針也強調，以「適當」貨幣政策打造強勁經濟的重要性；市場將這種措辭解讀為對快速正常化的警告。

這種矛盾可能形成自我強化的循環。政治阻力將延後日本央行行動的預期，使日圓走弱；日圓貶值推高通膨與進口商品成本；由此產生的壓力，最終又提高升息的必要性。在日本央行化解這項矛盾前，標售結果顯示投資人已要求主權債殖利率曲線反映相關風險。

海外資金流向進一步加重壓力。6月海外投資人淨賣出¥3.12兆、約$192億的日本債券，創2023年1月以來最大單月撤資，統計涵蓋至6月26日。由於當月有¥22.1兆主權債到期，贖回可能是部分原因，但資金流出也恰逢日圓下跌、日本央行購債減少及政府支出疑慮升高。

國內利率上升也在改變企業融資方式。日本企業上半年發行¥1兆可轉換公司債，為2004年以來同期最高。日本製鐵發行¥6,000億，創日本最大規模的可轉債交易；JX Advanced Metals發行¥2,500億，Advantest則完成一筆超額認購的$6.3億交易。傳統借款成本上升時，附加股票轉換權可讓發行人降低甚至免付票息。

投資需求相當強勁：日本製鐵的訂單規模達發行額的數倍，Advantest與JX交易的需求則超過發行規模8倍。不過，轉換可能稀釋現有股東權益，發行人股價也出現相應反應。日本製鐵宣布融資時下跌逾5%，JX Metals則下挫約17%。日本殖利率上升不僅改變主權債估值，也正在重塑企業籌資結構。

## 歐洲與亞洲面臨不同的通膨制約

歐洲央行的討論焦點，已從6月是否有必要升息，轉向後續再次升息所需的條件。總裁Christine Lagarde為上月決策辯護，表示中東供給衝擊開始擴散至經濟後，管理委員會採取的行動正確。她承認第二輪效應尚未出現，仍將已可見的間接成本轉嫁，與官員試圖防止的、更持久的薪資物價循環區分開來。

6月通膨降至2.8%，油價也回到戰前水準，使管理委員會立場分歧。首席經濟學家Philip Lane持續警告，先前的成本增幅可能延後傳導至薪資、食品與服務。愛沙尼亞央行總裁Ulo Kaasik認為，至少再升息一次是合理的。另一端，希臘央行總裁Yannis Stournaras主張暫時按兵不動；芬蘭央行總裁Olli Rehn未見重大第二輪效應，奧地利央行總裁Martin Kocher則表示眼前的通膨威脅已減弱。拉脫維亞央行總裁Martins Kazaks與斯洛維尼亞央行總裁Primoz Dolenc都認為7月無須急於行動。

最新勞動數據未能讓任何一方取得決定性依據。4月數據下修至6.2%後，歐元區5月失業率維持同一水準。失業人數較4月減少55,000人、較上年同期減少158,000人，降至1,098.6萬人，青年失業率則維持14.7%。勞動市場仍足以讓薪資持續性成為政策考量，卻沒有重新加速到迫使央行立即升息的程度。

住宅市場持續以不均衡的方式反映累積所得與融資條件。歐元區房價第1季上漲1%，較上年同期上漲4.7%，年增率低於前一季的5.1%。歐盟房價季增1.2%、年增5.1%。各國表現從芬蘭下跌2%到葡萄牙上漲17.8%不等，如此大的差異使政策官員難以對家庭財富與利率敏感度作出單一判斷。

英國央行決策委員Catherine Mann提出了更明確的條件門檻。她6月與多數委員一同投票支持將政策利率維持在3.75%，但表示，若通膨預期、企業定價行為或2027年薪資談判的基礎惡化，她準備支持採取「積極」升息。她未在6月支持升息，部分原因是當時較緊的市場條件已在抑制需求；不過，隨著市場對美國與伊朗達成協議的期待升高，這些條件已大幅放鬆。

Mann將下一步決策與能源價格、企業利潤率及薪資連結，而非只看最新的整體通膨數字。她警告，即使能源成本下降，企業仍可能維持較高售價，以重建利潤率。整體失業率上升也可能掩蓋個別產業較強的勞動市場狀況，使需求比總體數字所顯示的更具韌性。

南韓面對的是不同問題。6月整體通膨率由3.1%升至3.2%，符合預測，並創2023年12月以來最快增幅；核心通膨率維持2.5%。運輸成本較上年同期上升11.1%，休閒與文化上漲5.4%，食品與住宿以及家庭用品與服務則均上漲2.7%。

這項結果進一步強化韓國央行在7月16日會議前轉趨鷹派的立場。已有兩位理事支持立即升息，決策官員的討論也愈來愈集中於緊縮時點，而非是否需要進一步緊縮。6月半導體出貨量接近增至3倍，使經工作日調整的出口成長率逼近60%；政府同時協調企業對晶片製造與AI資料中心投入至少韓元1,350兆。出口需求強勁、韓元疲弱、房價上漲及核心通膨僵固，使升息理由不再只限於能源推升的整體通膨。

紐西蘭央行政策委員會在7月8日開會時仍將勢均力敵。央行在11月大選前不會再任命內部委員，因此維持3名內部委員與3名外部委員的配置。5月時，3名外部委員全數支持升息，總裁Anna Breman則以決定票支持維持利率不變。若分歧持續，未變的委員會結構將再次使總裁的判斷成為關鍵。

澳洲則提供區內成長轉弱的證據。經季節調整後，5月商品貿易餘額由4月的A$13.83億順差轉為A$30.18億逆差，惡化A$44.01億。出口下降6.9%至A$436.14億，主因非貨幣黃金出口減少35%；進口則增加2.6%至A$466.32億。

與此同時，房市下行已由雪梨與墨爾本向外擴散。雪梨房價第2季下跌3.2%，墨爾本下跌2.6%，阿德雷德、布里斯本及其他先前較具韌性的市場，動能也轉弱。負扣稅制度調整估計使部分投資人的借款能力降低20%至30%，較高的政策利率又進一步加重負擔能力限制。Bloomberg Economics估計，房價下跌可能使2026年下半年消費支出減少0.1%至0.3%；若勞動需求轉弱，澳洲央行的政策重點可能由持續通膨轉向成長。

## AI重新定價同時波及股票與投資級債券

美國大盤持穩之際，科技股賣壓進一步加劇。那斯達克100指數下跌1.61%，半導體指數下挫5.44%，使兩週跌幅擴至約12%。民生消費、公用事業與醫療保健類股上漲，抵銷科技股回落，標普500指數因而大致持平。VIX下跌2.65%至16.15，顯示這波集中式賣壓尚未演變為全面撤資。

壓力始於亞洲。SK Hynix與Samsung Electronics市值合計蒸發$2,900億，拖累韓國綜合股價指數下跌7.9%。市場傳出新的客製化晶片計畫，雲端運算競爭也加劇，促使投資人重新評估記憶體需求與資料中心建設能否達到預期。一檔與SK Hynix連結的香港槓桿基金規模已增至約$130億，分析師警告，其再平衡交易的規模足以放大標的股票及韓國股價指數的波動。

科技公司的借款規模異常龐大，使股票修正與固定收益市場的關聯日益密切。2026年至今，企業在各種幣別共發行約$2,200億AI相關債券，較2025年全年多62%。Amazon、Meta、Alphabet與Oracle四家超大規模雲端業者合計發行約$1,070億美元債券，Nvidia與SpaceX則在6月各發行$250億。

高評級科技債供給增加，以機械式方式改善了美國投資級債券指數的評級組成。AA級與A級證券目前占52%，高於2021年的約46%；BBB級占比則由46%降至41%。截至7月1日，投資級債券利差約為0.74個百分點，接近數十年低點。

表面上的品質改善，掩蓋了曝險日益集中於單一投資論述的問題。美國6家最大超大規模雲端業者計畫在2026年投入近$8,200億發展AI，較一年前預期高出近80%。目前現金產生能力相當可觀：Alphabet的營業現金流預計在2027年超過$2,500億，Nvidia未來5年自由現金流可能接近$1.5兆。然而，這些借款的前提是資料中心與模型收入能夠擴大至足以支撐相關資本投入。

風險不只來自景氣循環下的獲利波動。技術可能在20年期、30年期甚至100年期債券到期前便已過時；工程延誤、成本超支、電力限制、客戶不付款及合約未能續約，也都可能在發行人需要再融資前削弱投資報酬。Oracle已明確列出其中數項風險，企業AI應用調查也發現，實際成本節省經常低於最初目標。

最新市場走勢已初步區分發行人本身的品質與市場對AI題材的熱度。SpaceX債券上市後大幅走弱；市場擔心產能過剩，以及替代技術可能需要較少記憶體，也引發晶片股拋售。若AI資本支出退潮，受影響的不只超大規模雲端業者，還包括獲利日益依賴建設潮的半導體製造商、電力供應商、營造公司及其他受惠企業。

整體信用債市場仍然有序。LQD上漲0.17%、HYG上升0.15%、JNK上漲0.11%，EMB則增加0.19%。這些小幅漲勢與美國公債短端殖利率下降及整體風險偏好穩定一致，但仍無法確認現有利差是否足以補償科技曝險集中與未來大量發債的風險。

指數層面的平穩反應，本身也是信用債市場的重要議題。規模龐大且評級甚高的科技業借款人，一方面提高投資級債券指標的平均品質，另一方面也增加市場對同一資本支出週期的曝險。若AI收入不如預期，這個市場的利差仍可能全面擴大，儘管從統計上看，它比BBB級工業債與併購融資債券占比較高時更安全。即使基本面未惡化，只要持續增加的供給超過投資人需求，也可能迫使新債提供更大的發行讓利。

## 前端融資順利去化，新興亞洲吸引資金

美國財政部4週與8週期國庫券標售顯示，假期中斷交易前市場現金需求充裕。28天期國庫券得標金額為$850億，最高得標利率3.605%，投標倍數2.72。間接投標人取得獲接受競爭性投標的67.05%，直接投標人占3.75%，一級交易商占29.20%。債券於7月7日交割，8月4日到期。

56天期國庫券得標金額為$850.01億，最高得標利率3.650%，投標倍數2.70。間接投標人取得61.72%，直接投標人占3.90%，交易商占34.38%。這批債券同樣於7月7日交割，並在9月1日到期。由於沒有發行前交易殖利率作為參照，結果只能說明參與度與配售情況，無法判斷兩場標售相對當時市場水準是偏貴還是偏便宜。

合計$1,700億供給順利去化，沒有跡象顯示假期前出現融資壓力。這兩場標售接續同一交割日先前舉行的17週期國庫券標售，假期後還將迎來另一輪密集發債。結果顯示，短端現金吸收仍有秩序，與較長天期JGB遭拋售，以及美國長債未能跟隨2年期公債上漲，形成明確區別。

儘管聯準會仍有升息風險，新興亞洲本幣債券也持續吸引國際資金。6月流入泰國、印尼、印度與馬來西亞的海外資金合計達$82億，為兩年多來最高。美國與伊朗達成臨時協議後，區域本幣債券指數上漲0.2%；歐洲、中東與非洲市場大致持平，拉丁美洲則下跌0.6%。

相對較高的區域政策利率、油價下跌及外部收支狀況改善，均支撐這波資金流入。美國5年期公債殖利率與新興亞洲同天期殖利率的30天相關係數約為0.04，低於歐洲、中東與非洲的0.34及拉丁美洲的0.44。近期觀察到的敏感度較低，使亞洲本幣債券較不直接受到美國公債波動影響；不過，若聯準會立場再度轉鷹，衝擊仍會透過匯率傳導。

週四美元走弱改善了這項傳導條件。新興市場貨幣上漲0.2%，南非蘭特、匈牙利福林及數種拉丁美洲貨幣均走升。就業報告降低聯準會急於升息的必要，使貨幣得以上漲；與此同時，受到韓國科技股重挫拖累，新興市場股票下跌約2%。

這種分歧說明，區域債券資金流入不能被視為市場對所有亞洲資產投下信任票。本幣固定收益資產受惠於政策利差收益、能源成本下降及美元走弱，股票市場則承受AI部位高度集中的壓力。若油價或美國殖利率再度上升，兩類資產都將面臨挑戰，但作用機制不同：債券面對的是進口通膨與政策壓力，股票則承受估值與融資成本衝擊。

## 後市意涵

依SIFMA的美國獨立紀念日建議，美國固定收益市場7月3日休市，沒有完整的美國公債交易時段可消化新資訊。亞洲與歐洲市場仍然開市，6月服務業與綜合採購經理人指數終值，將提供美國以外地區就業、需求及價格壓力的最新線索。在10年期公債標售疲弱的影響仍未消退之際，日本約¥3.8兆的3個月期國庫券標售將檢驗短端需求。

假期後美國首項重大考驗將於7月6日到來，6月ISM服務業指數與紐約聯準銀行全球供應鏈壓力指數均在美東時間上午10時公布。服務業招聘與價格將顯示就業放緩是否擴及經濟最大部門；物流成本則可反映荷姆茲海峽航運改善，是否正將供給衝擊的緩解傳導至更廣泛領域。同日稍早公布的歐元區5月生產者物價與零售銷售，將更新歐洲央行政策分歧背後的上游通膨與家庭需求平衡。

美國財政部7月6日恢復發債，將標售$920億13週期及$790億26週期國庫券，兩者均於7月9日交割。7月7日另有$900億6週期國庫券、$520億52週期國庫券及$580億新發3年期公債。這是非農就業數據將市場完全反映的聯準會升息時點推遲至12月後，首次舉行附息公債標售，將檢驗買方是否接受新的短端殖利率結構，而不要求更大的發行讓利。

全球長天期債券更關鍵的事件，是日本7月7日約¥6,000億的30年期公債標售。此前10年期標售需求疲弱、20年期殖利率上升9.5個基點，海外投資人大量賣出日本債券，企業長期通膨預期也創新高。在財政與匯率疑慮持續之際，保險公司及其他國內投資人的需求，將顯示較高殖利率是否足以穩定超長端。7月9日接著標售約¥2.5兆5年期公債，檢驗殖利率曲線中對日本央行正常化時點更敏感的區段。

美國5月貿易數據與紐約聯準銀行6月消費者預期調查，將於7月7日美東時間上午8時30分及11時公布。Daly仍保留以更強力手段因應持續價格壓力的可能，而就業數據疲弱已降低7月升息的急迫性，因此家庭通膨預期格外重要。調查可釐清油價下跌是否已反映在消費者展望中，或關稅與服務成本是否仍使預期維持高檔。

美國財政部7月8日將增額發行$390億10年期公債，檢驗指標殖利率未因就業數據疲弱而下降後的長天期需求。6月16日至17日FOMC會議紀要將於美東時間下午2時公布。投資人將關注9位預測2026年至少升息一次的官員所持理由、決策委員對通膨疑慮的廣度，以及委員會如何評估其後於6月僅增加57,000個職位的勞動市場。

本輪附息債券發行週期將於7月9日結束。美東時間上午8時30分公布每週失業救濟金數據後，財政部將增額發行$220億30年期公債。亞洲交易時段稍早將公布中國6月消費者與生產者物價，日本也將標售5年期公債。這些事件將綜合檢驗長天期主權債需求，並提供亞洲商品通膨、美國勞動市場流動及全球通膨降溫持續性的證據。

油價仍是聯準會、歐洲央行、英國央行及亞洲央行政策前景的共同條件。隨著荷姆茲海峽油輪通行恢復、美國與伊朗談判取得進展，WTI與布蘭特原油單月均跌逾24%，但通過海峽的安全持續性與成本仍有疑問。若情勢持續正常化，整體通膨可望下降，央行也能有更多時間評估薪資與服務價格。若運輸再度受阻，進口價格壓力將最快在日本與南韓回升，也會挑戰目前短端已反映的聯準會延後升息路徑。

overall_summary.headline: 就業數據疲弱壓低美國公債短端，長端殖利率卻拒絕下行
overall_summary.session_narrative:
6月非農就業人數僅增加57,000人，不及113,000人的預測，前2個月數據也遭下修，帶動美國公債殖利率曲線在SIFMA建議的美東時間下午2時提前收市前轉陡。2年期殖利率下跌3.9個基點至4.138%，10年期卻上升0.5個基點至4.485%，30年期增加1.5個基點至4.986%；2年期與10年期利差擴大4.4個基點至34.7個基點。

就業數據不及預期與空頭回補，使市場隱含的聯準會7月升息機率由約33%降至約20%，完全反映升息1碼的時點也由10月延後至12月。不過，勞動參與率下降使失業率降至4.2%，初領失業救濟金人數維持低檔，工廠出貨也有所增加。10年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率同步微升，顯示投資人只是延後預期中的緊縮，而非放棄限制性政策可能持續的看法。

日本10年期公債標售需求疲弱，加重全球長天期債券壓力。財政擴張、日圓疲弱，以及日本央行漸進升息可能讓通膨壓力持續的疑慮，推動指標JGB殖利率上升7個基點至2.77%。收市較晚的美國風險資產表現分歧：大盤大致持穩，科技股與半導體股卻大幅下挫，凸顯AI資本支出、龐大投資級債券供給與長期信用風險之間日益緊密的關聯。
overall_summary.summary: 6月非農就業僅增加57,000人，使市場完全反映的聯準會升息時點由10月延後至12月，並壓低2年期殖利率；但初領失業救濟金人數穩健、失業率下降，加上通膨、供給與期限溢價疑慮持續，使較長天期美國公債殖利率未能下行。

section_summaries.summary: 縮短的美國公債交易時段呈現明確的曲線陡峭化，而非全面的長天期債券漲勢。非農就業疲弱與短端空頭回補降低近期聯準會風險，但失業率下降、失業救濟金申請穩健及工廠活動，避免經濟驟然收縮成為市場主流解讀。實質殖利率上升、通膨風險持續、主權債供給壓力及日本標售疲弱，使長端未能跟隨政策敏感區段上漲。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries steepened on July 2 after a sharp slowdown in U.S. hiring reduced the urgency of another Federal Reserve increase but failed to generate a broad duration rally. In daily observations for the shortened session, the 2-year yield fell 3.9 basis points to 4.138%, while the 10-year edged 0.5 basis point higher to 4.485% and the 30-year rose 1.5 basis points to 4.986%. The 2s10s curve widened 4.4 basis points to 34.7 basis points, and 2s30s increased 5.4 basis points to 84.8 basis points. The session had a SIFMA-recommended early close at 2:00 p.m. ET ahead of U.S. Independence Day.

Nonfarm payrolls rose only 57,000 in June, versus the 113,000 median forecast, and the preceding 2 months were revised lower. The unemployment rate nevertheless fell to 4.2% because labor-force participation dropped. The mixed composition encouraged investors to remove some near-term tightening risk without treating the release as evidence of an abrupt downturn. The implied probability of a July increase fell to about 20% from roughly 33% before the data, and the first fully priced quarter-point move shifted to December from October.

The curve’s response captured the distinction. Payroll weakness and short-covering benefited the policy-sensitive sector, but the 10-year real yield still rose 0.3 basis point to 2.246%, and the 10-year breakeven increased 0.2 basis point to 2.239%. Claims remained low, factory shipments increased, and the June employment report’s lower jobless rate complicated an otherwise soft payroll headline. Investors delayed the expected Fed move rather than abandoning the view that restrictive policy may persist.

Oil offered further relief from the immediate inflation shock but no fresh collapse in prices. WTI settled 0.16% higher at $68.69 and Brent gained 0.32% to $71.80 after both touched their lowest levels since February; each remained more than 24% lower over the month. The dollar index fell 0.52% to 100.86, while gold futures rose 1.09% to $4,112.70. Those moves were consistent with a less urgent Fed path, although the long end’s failure to rally showed that lower near-term policy risk did not remove real-rate, supply or term-premium pressure.

Japan reinforced the global duration constraint. A weak 10-year government-bond auction pushed the benchmark yield 7 basis points higher to 2.77% and the 20-year rate up 9.5 basis points to 3.76%. Investors were confronting a combination of fiscal expansion, a deeply weakened yen and concern that gradual Bank of Japan tightening may allow inflation pressure to persist. The result followed stronger corporate conditions and record long-run inflation expectations in the Tankan, increasing the case for another BOJ move even as the government favors caution.

Risk assets delivered a divided response rather than a conventional growth scare. The S&P 500 finished essentially unchanged and the Dow rose 1.1%, but the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.61% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 5.44%. Broad listed credit funds posted small gains, while emerging-market currencies benefited from the weaker dollar. The separation between stable broad risk appetite and a concentrated technology selloff mattered for bonds because AI-related borrowers are now responsible for a large share of investment-grade supply. Softer payrolls eased the Fed constraint; they did not settle whether the capital-intensive technology cycle, sovereign issuance and persistent inflation risks will keep longer yields elevated.

## Payrolls Push the Expected Fed Increase Toward December

June’s 57,000 payroll increase was lower than all but one forecast in the surveyed range and followed downward revisions to the preceding 2 months. The slowdown interrupted the stronger hiring momentum that had emerged earlier in the year. Leisure and hospitality recorded its largest payroll decline since 2020, providing a more specific sign of weakness than the aggregate result alone.

The fall in unemployment to 4.2% prevented the release from reading as an unambiguous deterioration. Labor-force participation declined, allowing the jobless rate to fall even as hiring slowed. For monetary policy, that combination weakens the case for an immediate increase but does not establish the kind of broad labor-market contraction that would normally produce a sustained rally across the Treasury curve.

Weekly claims reinforced the distinction between slower hiring and widespread layoffs. Initial claims slipped by 1,000 to 215,000 in the week ended June 27, with the preceding week revised to 216,000 from 215,000. The 4-week average declined by 2,500 to 222,000. Insured unemployment rose by 2,000 to 1.814 million in the week ended June 20, and its 4-week average increased by 10,750 to 1.803 million, while the insured unemployment rate held at 1.2%.

The claims figures suggest that workers who lose jobs may be taking somewhat longer to find new employment, but employers have not begun cutting staff at a pace associated with a rapid contraction. That helps explain why the front end rallied while longer maturities remained firm in yield: the data reduced the probability of near-term tightening more clearly than they reduced the expected duration of restrictive policy.

Short-covering amplified the 2-year move. Bearish positions had accumulated around the possibility of a July increase following the Fed’s June meeting, when 9 of 18 policymakers projected at least one increase during 2026. With the July probability falling to about 20%, investors who had expected a stronger labor report had reason to unwind front-end shorts. The resulting 2-year rally therefore reflected both a change in the reaction-function evidence and the positioning carried into the release.

San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly supplied a separate policy signal after the employment report. Daly said the current stance was slightly restrictive and should bring inflation lower. She welcomed the retreat in oil after the U.S.-Iran ceasefire but emphasized that the outlook remained unusually uncertain and that persistent inflation could require a more forceful response. Her position preserved conditional tightening rather than endorsing the market’s most dovish interpretation of payrolls.

Daly also resisted changing the Fed’s objectives as Chair Kevin Warsh reviews its operations and analytical framework. She said the institution could modernize how it assesses the economy without moving the goalposts for maximum employment and price stability. That distinction matters because the Fed’s preferred inflation measure had risen 4.1% from a year earlier in May, its fastest pace since April 2023. One weak payroll report reduces the case for haste, but it does not eliminate the inflation problem that produced the June tightening projections.

May factory data added another reason not to equate the employment miss with an economy-wide break. New orders fell 1.3%, or $8.5 billion, to $657.4 billion after a 5.3% increase in April. Shipments rose 1.6% to $653.2 billion, however, and unfilled orders increased 0.6% to $1.5795 trillion. Inventories gained 0.2% to $962 billion. The unfilled-orders-to-shipments ratio declined to 6.91 from 6.95, while the inventories-to-shipments ratio fell to 1.47 from 1.49.

The result showed softer new demand after April’s surge but continued production and backlog growth. Combined with low initial claims, it supported a slower-growth interpretation rather than a sudden collapse. The June payroll report changed the timing of the expected Fed response most decisively: the market continued to price one quarter-point increase during 2026, but no longer expected it before December.

Treasury trading activity was lower in the abbreviated session. FINRA recorded $848.4 billion of par activity across 316,299 trades, down 31.5% from July 1. Nominal-coupon activity fell 28.9% to $635.3 billion, and TIPS activity declined 43.1% to $15.3 billion. The reductions were consistent with the shortened holiday schedule, but the front-end repricing was still substantial enough to steepen the curve materially.

## Japan’s Weak Auction Exposes the Cost of Gradual Normalization

Japan’s 10-year auction delivered the day’s clearest sovereign-demand disappointment. The bid-to-cover ratio fell to 3.13 from 3.53 at the previous sale and below its 3.33 average over the past year. The auction tail widened to its largest since April, and the lowest accepted price came in well below pre-sale estimates. Market makers took little more than their required allotments, signaling limited willingness to absorb benchmark duration at prevailing yields.

The secondary-market reaction was immediate. The 10-year JGB yield climbed 7 basis points to 2.77%, while the 20-year rose 9.5 basis points to 3.76%. The weakness was not simply a mechanical response to the Bank of Japan’s June rate increase to 1%. Investors were also demanding compensation for fiscal expansion, continued yen depreciation and the risk that the BOJ remains behind the inflation process.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government is pursuing large spending plans and has set a goal of expanding nominal GDP to $6.8 trillion in the fiscal year beginning April 2040. Investors are also waiting to see whether the government proceeds with suspending the sales tax on food and beverages. Those ambitions arrive as government debt exceeds 200% of GDP and as higher yields gradually raise the cost of refinancing the existing debt stock.

The yen’s weakness intensifies the dilemma. It traded near 161.30 per dollar in the subsequent Asian session after reaching levels last seen in 1986. Currency depreciation raises imported energy and material costs, while political pressure for gradual tightening leaves the BOJ with less room to close the rate differential quickly. Intervention earlier in the year temporarily strengthened the currency, but it did not remove the policy and fiscal conditions behind the decline.

Current domestic evidence is making caution harder to sustain. The June Tankan showed business confidence at its strongest in 8 years despite the Middle East conflict. An index of companies’ financial positions improved for the first time in a year, and large firms reported better conditions for issuing commercial paper. The survey therefore undercut the argument that earlier BOJ increases had already impaired corporate financing.

Longer-run inflation expectations in the Tankan rose to 2.6%, the highest in the series dating to 2014. Markets now assign more than a 60% probability to another BOJ increase by October, whereas economists had previously clustered around a roughly 6-month interval that implied December. Some forecasters have moved October into their base case and see a growing possibility of September.

Politics still points in the opposite direction. Takaichi has consistently favored accommodative policy, and her BOJ appointees Ayano Sato and Toichiro Asada are regarded as sympathetic to easier settings. Asada cast the only dissent against the June increase, while Sato has said that an inflationary norm is not yet firmly established. The government’s economic guidelines have also stressed the importance of “appropriate” monetary policy for building a strong economy, language markets have interpreted as a warning against rapid normalization.

That tension can become self-reinforcing. Expectations that political resistance will delay the BOJ weaken the yen; the weaker yen raises inflation and the cost of imported goods; and the resulting pressure increases the eventual need for higher rates. The auction showed that investors are already charging the sovereign curve for that risk before the BOJ resolves it.

Foreign flows added to the pressure. Overseas investors sold a net ¥3.12 trillion, or $19.2 billion, of Japanese bonds in June, the largest monthly withdrawal since January 2023. The figures cover the period through June 26. Redemptions probably contributed, because ¥22.1 trillion of sovereign securities matured during the month, but the outflow coincided with the yen’s slide, reduced BOJ purchases and rising government-spending concerns.

Higher domestic rates are also altering corporate funding. Japanese companies issued ¥1 trillion of convertible bonds during the first half, the most for that period since 2004. Nippon Steel’s ¥600 billion transaction was the country’s largest convertible issue, while JX Advanced Metals sold ¥250 billion and Advantest completed a $630 million oversubscribed deal. The ability to attach an equity option allows issuers to reduce or eliminate coupons as conventional borrowing costs rise.

Investor demand has been strong: the Nippon Steel sale attracted orders many times the offered amount, while the Advantest and JX transactions drew demand exceeding 8 times their size. Yet conversion can dilute existing shareholders, and issuer stock prices have reacted accordingly. Nippon Steel fell more than 5% when it announced its financing, and JX Metals dropped about 17%. Rising Japanese yields are therefore changing both sovereign valuations and the structure through which companies raise capital.

## Europe and Asia Produce Different Inflation Constraints

The European Central Bank’s debate moved from the necessity of June’s increase to the conditions for any subsequent move. President Christine Lagarde defended last month’s decision, saying the Governing Council had acted correctly after the Middle East supply shock began spreading through the economy. She acknowledged that second-round effects had not yet materialized, preserving the distinction between indirect cost pass-through already visible and the more persistent wage-price process officials are trying to prevent.

June inflation’s decline to 2.8% and oil’s return to pre-war levels have divided the Council. Chief Economist Philip Lane continues to warn that earlier cost increases may reach wages, food and services with a lag. Estonian Governor Ulo Kaasik regards at least one more increase as reasonable. At the other end, Greek Governor Yannis Stournaras favors holding for now, while Finland’s Olli Rehn sees no major second-round effects and Austria’s Martin Kocher says the immediate inflation threat has diminished. Latvia’s Martins Kazaks and Slovenia’s Primoz Dolenc see no urgency to act in July.

Current labor data gave neither side a decisive result. Euro-area unemployment held at 6.2% in May after April was revised down to the same rate. The number of unemployed people fell by 55,000 from April and by 158,000 from a year earlier, to 10.986 million. Youth unemployment remained at 14.7%. The labor market is firm enough to keep wage persistence relevant, but it did not provide a fresh acceleration that would compel an immediate increase.

Housing continues to transmit accumulated income and financing conditions unevenly. Euro-area house prices rose 1% in Q1 and 4.7% from a year earlier, down from a 5.1% annual pace in the previous quarter. EU prices increased 1.2% quarterly and 5.1% annually. National changes ranged from a 2% decline in Finland to a 17.8% increase in Portugal, a dispersion that complicates a single assessment of household wealth and rate sensitivity.

Bank of England policymaker Catherine Mann set a more explicit conditional threshold. Mann, who voted with the majority to hold the policy rate at 3.75% in June, said she was prepared to support an “activist” increase if inflation expectations, price-setting or the foundations of 2027 wage negotiations deteriorate. She had refrained from backing a June increase partly because tighter market conditions were already restraining demand, but said those conditions had loosened substantially as hopes for a U.S.-Iran settlement improved.

Mann’s position links the next decision to energy prices, corporate margins and wages rather than to the latest headline reading alone. She warned that companies may retain higher prices to rebuild margins even if energy costs moderate. Rising aggregate unemployment also may conceal stronger conditions in particular industries, leaving demand more resilient than broad figures suggest.

South Korea faces a different problem: headline inflation accelerated to 3.2% in June from 3.1%, matching forecasts and reaching its fastest pace since December 2023. Core inflation held at 2.5%. Transportation costs rose 11.1% from a year earlier and recreation and culture increased 5.4%, while food and lodging and household goods and services each gained 2.7%.

The result reinforces the Bank of Korea’s hawkish turn before its July 16 meeting. Two board members had already favored an immediate increase, and policymakers are increasingly debating timing rather than the principle of further restraint. Semiconductor shipments almost tripled in June, helping working-day-adjusted export growth approach 60%, while the government is coordinating at least 1,350 trillion won of corporate investment in chip fabrication and AI data centers. Strong export demand, a weak won, rising home prices and sticky core inflation all broaden the case for tightening beyond the energy-driven headline.

New Zealand’s policy committee will remain evenly divided when it meets July 8. The Reserve Bank will not appoint an additional internal member before the November election, leaving 3 internal and 3 external members. In May, all 3 external members favored an increase, and Governor Anna Breman used her casting vote to hold. The unchanged structure makes the governor’s judgment decisive again if the split persists.

Australia supplied weaker regional growth evidence. Its seasonally adjusted goods balance swung to an A$3.018 billion deficit in May from an A$1.383 billion surplus in April, a deterioration of A$4.401 billion. Exports fell 6.9% to A$43.614 billion, led by a 35% decline in non-monetary-gold exports, while imports rose 2.6% to A$46.632 billion.

That release arrived as a housing downturn spread beyond Sydney and Melbourne. Sydney prices fell 3.2% in the June quarter and Melbourne declined 2.6%, while momentum weakened in Adelaide, Brisbane and other previously resilient markets. Changes to negative-gearing treatment have reduced some investors’ borrowing capacity by an estimated 20%-30%, and higher policy rates have compounded the affordability constraint. Bloomberg Economics estimates the housing decline could subtract 0.1%-0.3% from consumer spending during the second half of 2026, potentially shifting the Reserve Bank of Australia’s emphasis from persistent inflation toward growth if labor demand weakens.

## AI Repricing Reaches Both Equities and Investment-Grade Debt

The technology selloff deepened even as the broader U.S. equity market held steady. The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.61%, and the semiconductor index lost 5.44%, extending its 2-week decline to about 12%. The S&P 500 was essentially unchanged because gains in consumer staples, utilities and healthcare offset the technology retreat. The VIX fell 2.65% to 16.15, indicating that the concentrated selloff did not become a general liquidation.

The pressure began in Asia, where SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics lost a combined $290 billion in market value and drove the Kospi down 7.9%. Investors were reassessing whether memory demand and data-center construction can meet expectations after reports of new custom-chip plans and additional cloud-computing competition. A Hong Kong leveraged fund tied to SK Hynix has grown to about $13 billion, large enough for analysts to warn that its rebalancing can amplify moves in the underlying shares and the Korean index.

The equity correction has become increasingly relevant to fixed income because technology companies are borrowing at exceptional scale. Companies have sold about $220 billion of AI-related bonds across currencies in 2026, 62% more than during all of 2025. Four hyperscalers—Amazon, Meta, Alphabet and Oracle—accounted for about $107 billion of dollar issuance, while Nvidia and SpaceX each sold $25 billion in June.

High-quality technology supply has mechanically improved the rating composition of the U.S. investment-grade index. AA and A securities now make up 52%, up from roughly 46% in 2021, while BBB exposure has fallen to 41% from 46%. Investment-grade spreads stood near 0.74 percentage point on July 1, close to multidecade lows.

That apparent improvement masks a growing concentration in a single investment thesis. The 6 largest U.S. hyperscalers plan to spend almost $820 billion on AI during 2026, nearly 80% more than anticipated a year ago. Current cash generation is substantial—Alphabet’s operating cash flow is forecast to exceed $250 billion in 2027, and Nvidia’s free cash flow could approach $1.5 trillion over 5 years—but the borrowing assumes that data-center and model revenue will scale sufficiently to justify the capital.

The risks extend beyond cyclical earnings. Technology may become obsolete before 20-, 30- or even 100-year bonds mature. Construction delays, cost overruns, power constraints, customer nonpayment and failure to renew contracts can weaken returns before issuers face refinancing. Oracle has explicitly identified several of those risks, while surveys of corporate AI deployment have found that cost savings frequently fall short of initial objectives.

The latest market action provided an early distinction between issuer quality and thematic enthusiasm. SpaceX bonds weakened sharply after their debut, while chip equities sold off on concern about excess capacity and alternative technologies requiring less memory. A retreat in AI capital expenditure would affect not only hyperscalers but also semiconductor manufacturers, power suppliers, construction firms and other beneficiaries whose earnings increasingly depend on the buildout.

Broad credit remained orderly. LQD gained 0.17%, HYG rose 0.15%, JNK added 0.11% and EMB increased 0.19%. Those small price advances were consistent with lower short Treasury yields and stable aggregate risk appetite. They did not resolve whether spreads adequately compensate investors for technology concentration or the volume of future issuance.

The benign index-level response is itself part of the credit story. Large, highly rated technology borrowers raise the average quality of investment-grade benchmarks even as they increase exposure to the same capital-spending cycle. If AI revenues disappoint, spread widening could occur across a market that looks statistically safer than it did when BBB industrial and acquisition debt represented a larger share. Continued supply alone may also require wider concessions if investor demand fails to keep pace.

## Front-End Funding Clears as Emerging Asia Draws Capital

Treasury’s 4- and 8-week auctions showed substantial cash demand before the holiday interruption. The 28-day bill auction accepted $85.000 billion at a 3.605% high rate with a 2.72 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders took 67.05% of accepted competitive tenders, direct bidders 3.75% and primary dealers 29.20%. The bills settle July 7 and mature August 4.

The 56-day sale accepted $85.001 billion at a 3.650% high rate with a 2.70 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders received 61.72%, directs 3.90% and dealers 34.38%. Those securities also settle July 7 and mature September 1. Without a when-issued reference, the results establish participation and allocation rather than whether either auction priced rich or cheap to prevailing levels.

The combined $170 billion of accepted supply cleared without evidence of holiday funding stress. It followed the earlier 17-week bill sale on the same settlement date and preceded another heavy post-holiday auction calendar. The results help separate orderly front-end cash absorption from the selloff in longer JGBs and the failure of long Treasuries to follow the 2-year rally.

Emerging Asian local bonds were also attracting international capital despite residual Fed tightening risk. Combined foreign inflows to Thailand, Indonesia, India and Malaysia reached $8.2 billion in June, the highest in more than 2 years. A regional local-currency bond index gained 0.2% after the interim U.S.-Iran agreement, compared with little change in Europe, the Middle East and Africa and a 0.6% decline in Latin America.

The flow has been supported by relatively high regional policy rates, lower oil and stronger external balances. The 30-day correlation between 5-year U.S. yields and comparable emerging-Asian yields was about 0.04, versus 0.34 for Europe, the Middle East and Africa and 0.44 for Latin America. That lower observed sensitivity has made Asian local debt less directly exposed to recent Treasury volatility, although another hawkish Fed shift would still transmit through currencies.

Thursday’s weaker dollar improved that channel. Emerging-market currencies rose 0.2%, with the South African rand, Hungarian forint and several Latin American currencies gaining. The payroll report removed some urgency from Fed tightening and allowed currencies to rally even as emerging-market equities fell about 2% under the weight of the Korean technology rout.

The divergence showed why the regional bond inflow cannot be treated as a broad vote of confidence in every Asian asset. Local fixed income benefited from policy carry, cheaper energy and dollar weakness, while equity markets confronted concentrated AI positioning. A renewed rise in oil or U.S. yields would challenge both, but through different mechanisms: imported inflation and policy pressure for bonds, and valuation and financing costs for equities.

## Forward Market Significance

U.S. fixed-income markets are closed July 3 under SIFMA’s Independence Day recommendation, leaving no completed Treasury session to absorb new information. Asian and European markets remain open, with June final services and composite purchasing-managers’ indexes providing the next readings on employment, demand and price pressure outside the United States. Japan’s roughly ¥3.8 trillion 3-month bill auction offers a front-end demand check while the weak 10-year result remains fresh.

The first major U.S. post-holiday test arrives July 6 with June ISM services and the New York Fed’s Global Supply Chain Pressure Index at 10:00 ET. Services hiring and prices will help determine whether the payroll slowdown extends into the economy’s largest sector, while logistics costs will show whether improving Hormuz traffic is translating into broader relief from the supply shock. Euro-area May producer prices and retail sales, released earlier that day, will update the balance between pipeline inflation and household demand behind the ECB’s widening policy debate.

Treasury supply resumes July 6 with $92 billion of 13-week bills and $79 billion of 26-week bills, both settling July 9. July 7 brings $90 billion of 6-week bills, $52 billion of 52-week bills and a $58 billion new 3-year note. The 3-year sale is the first coupon auction after payrolls shifted the fully priced Fed increase to December and will test whether buyers accept the new front-end yield structure without requiring a larger concession.

Japan’s approximately ¥600 billion 30-year auction on July 7 is the more consequential global duration event. It follows the weak 10-year sale, a 9.5-basis-point increase in the 20-year yield, large foreign bond sales and record corporate inflation expectations. Demand from insurers and other domestic investors will indicate whether higher yields are sufficient to stabilize the super-long sector as fiscal and currency concerns persist. A roughly ¥2.5 trillion 5-year sale follows July 9, testing the part of the curve more directly exposed to the timing of BOJ normalization.

U.S. May trade and the New York Fed’s June Survey of Consumer Expectations arrive July 7 at 08:30 and 11:00 ET. Household inflation expectations will be particularly important after Daly kept open the possibility of a forceful response to persistent price pressure and after payroll weakness reduced the urgency of a July move. The release can clarify whether lower oil is reaching consumers’ outlook or whether tariffs and service costs are keeping expectations elevated.

The $39 billion 10-year Treasury reopening on July 8 will test long-duration demand after the benchmark yield failed to rally on weak payrolls. The June 16-17 FOMC minutes follow at 2:00 p.m. ET. Investors will look for the reasoning behind the 9 officials who projected at least one 2026 increase, the breadth of concern about inflation and the Committee’s assessment of a labor market that has since produced only 57,000 June jobs.

The coupon cycle ends July 9 with a $22 billion 30-year reopening after weekly claims at 08:30 ET. China’s June consumer and producer prices arrive earlier in the Asian day, alongside a Japanese 5-year auction. Together, those events will test demand for long sovereign duration against evidence on Asian goods inflation, U.S. labor flows and the persistence of global disinflation.

Oil remains the common condition across the Fed, ECB, BOE and Asian policy outlooks. WTI and Brent have fallen more than 24% over the month as tanker traffic through Hormuz recovered and U.S.-Iran talks advanced, but questions remain over the durability and cost of passage through the strait. Continued normalization would support lower headline inflation and give central banks more time to assess wages and services. Renewed disruption would restore imported-price pressure most quickly in Japan and South Korea, while challenging the delayed Fed path now embedded in the front end.

section_summaries.summary: The shortened Treasury session produced a clear steepening rather than a broad duration rally. Soft payrolls and front-end short-covering reduced near-term Fed risk, but the lower unemployment rate, firm claims and factory activity kept a sudden contraction from becoming the dominant reading. Higher real yields, persistent inflation risk, sovereign supply pressure and Japan’s weak auction left the long end resistant to the policy-sensitive rally.

section_summaries.market_read: Position unwinds amplified the 2-year rally after the probability of a July increase fell to about 20%.
section_summaries.section_title: Payrolls Push the Expected Fed Increase Toward December
section_summaries.summary: June payrolls rose 57,000 and prior months were revised lower, but unemployment fell to 4.2% as participation declined. Initial claims remained low, shipments and backlogs grew, and Daly retained the option of a forceful response to persistent inflation. The market still priced one quarter-point Fed increase in 2026, but moved the first fully priced step to December from October.

section_summaries.market_read: Political resistance to BOJ tightening can weaken the yen, lift imported inflation and raise the eventual cost of normalization.
section_summaries.section_title: Japan’s Weak Auction Exposes the Cost of Gradual Normalization
section_summaries.summary: Japan’s 10-year auction drew weaker demand and pushed 10- and 20-year yields sharply higher as investors charged more for fiscal expansion, yen depreciation and delayed BOJ normalization. Strong corporate conditions and record 2.6% long-run inflation expectations strengthened the case for another increase, while political resistance sustained the risk of a weaker yen and more imported inflation. Rising yields are also driving companies toward convertible bonds.

section_summaries.section_title: Europe and Asia Produce Different Inflation Constraints
section_summaries.summary: ECB officials split over whether June’s increase needs a sequel as inflation eased to 2.8% without clear second-round effects, while the BOE’s Mann tied further tightening to expectations, pricing and wages. South Korea’s 3.2% inflation, strong chip exports and weak won reinforced its hawkish turn. New Zealand faces another potential committee split, while Australia’s trade deficit and spreading housing downturn strengthened its growth risk.

section_summaries.market_read: Index quality can improve even as dependence on AI spending and future bond supply makes credit risk more concentrated.
section_summaries.section_title: AI Repricing Reaches Both Equities and Investment-Grade Debt
section_summaries.summary: A concentrated technology selloff left broad U.S. equities stable but exposed fixed income to the scale of AI financing. AI-related bond issuance reached about $220 billion in 2026 as hyperscalers planned almost $820 billion of spending. Highly rated borrowers have improved the investment-grade index’s rating mix, yet they have also concentrated credit exposure in one capital-spending cycle whose returns face construction, power, technology and customer risks.

section_summaries.market_read: Asian local bonds showed low recent sensitivity to U.S. yields, though a hawkish Fed shift would still transmit through currencies.
section_summaries.section_title: Front-End Funding Clears as Emerging Asia Draws Capital
section_summaries.summary: Treasury’s combined $170 billion of 4- and 8-week bill supply cleared with substantial cash demand and no sign of holiday funding stress. Foreign inflows into Thai, Indonesian, Indian and Malaysian local bonds reached $8.2 billion in June, supported by carry, lower oil and stronger external balances. A weaker dollar helped currencies even as the Korean technology rout weighed on emerging-market equities.

After the July 3 U.S. market closure, services activity and inflation expectations will test whether payroll weakness justifies the delayed Fed path. Japanese and U.S. auctions will probe demand for duration under fiscal, currency and supply pressure, while oil and Hormuz traffic remain the shared inflation condition across major central banks.

overall_summary.headline: Weak payrolls pull down the Treasury front end, but long yields resist
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries steepened into the SIFMA-recommended 2:00 p.m. ET early close after June payrolls rose only 57,000, missing the 113,000 forecast, with the preceding 2 months revised lower. The 2-year yield fell 3.9 basis points to 4.138%, but the 10-year rose 0.5 basis point to 4.485% and the 30-year increased 1.5 basis points to 4.986%. The 2s10s curve widened 4.4 basis points to 34.7 basis points.

The payroll miss and short-covering reduced the implied probability of a July Fed increase to about 20% from roughly 33% and shifted the first fully priced quarter-point move to December from October. Yet unemployment fell to 4.2% as participation declined, initial claims remained low and factory shipments increased. The 10-year real yield and breakeven also edged higher, showing that investors delayed the expected tightening rather than abandoning the prospect of restrictive policy.

A weak Japanese 10-year bond auction reinforced the pressure on global duration, sending the benchmark JGB yield 7 basis points higher to 2.77% amid fiscal expansion, yen weakness and concern that gradual BOJ tightening will allow inflation pressure to persist. Later-closing U.S. risk assets were divided: broad equities held near steady while technology and semiconductor shares fell sharply, highlighting the growing link between AI capital spending, heavy investment-grade issuance and longer-term credit risk.
overall_summary.summary: June’s 57,000 payroll gain pushed the first fully priced Fed increase from October to December and lowered the 2-year yield, while firm claims, a lower unemployment rate and persistent inflation, supply and term-premium concerns kept longer Treasury yields from rallying.
